name: Dye transport
question: How much apparent mixing comes from stirring and how much from diffusion?

derived.label: grid
derived.note: periodic box L = 2π; the end time does not depend on the resolution

derived.label: time step
derived.note: advection CFL; the viscous term is integrated exactly

plots.title: Dye mixing
plots.explain: Variance of the dye concentration over the domain (absolute). Stirring alone cannot reduce the variance of a conserved scalar; the decay seen here comes from molecular diffusion (κ = 0.0004) plus the numerical diffusion of the bilinear semi-Lagrangian scheme once filaments thin below the grid. Compare stirring strength 0.0 with 0 (diffusion only) and κ = 0 (stirring only) to separate the two.

mix_diffusion.name: Dye: Diffusion Only
mix_diffusion.question: How fast does diffusion alone smooth the bands?

layers.title: The question
layers.text: How fast does diffusion alone smooth the bands?

layers.title: What the colours and motion show
layers.text: The same bands with the stirring switched off. Each band decays as a pure diffusion problem whose solution is known.

layers.title: One change to try
items: Change κ and the number of bands: the decay rate scales as κ·(band wavenumber)².

layers.title: What to measure
layers.text: A smooth, exponential decay of the variance.

layers.title: Physical explanation
layers.text: With the stirring switched off the dye simply diffuses: each band decays at the rate κ·m² of its wavenumber m, so the fundamental of the stripes decays as exp(−κm²t) and the variance as exp(−2κm²t). This scene isolates physical diffusion from the stretching and folding of the stirred scenes.

layers.title: Equations, symbols and assumptions
layers.text:
• c — the dye concentration (a passive scalar; it does not affect the flow)
• u — the turbulent velocity stirring it, from the spectral solver
• (u·∇)c — advection: the flow carrying the dye and stretching it into filaments
• κ∇²c — molecular diffusion, small, smoothing only the very finest filaments
• ∇·u = 0 — the stirring flow is incompressible (area-preserving)

layers.title: Initial and boundary conditions (this preset)
layers.ic: Alternating horizontal dye bands (0/1) with the chosen number of stripes; no flow.
layers.bc: Periodic in both directions; the stirring velocity is zero.

layers.title: Numerical method, checks and limitations
layers.text: The turbulent velocity comes from the same spectral vorticity solver; the dye is a passive scalar advected by it with periodic bilinear semi-Lagrangian transport (unconditionally stable) and a touch of spectral diffusion.
layers.checks: Analytical comparison: for stripes with wavenumber m the variance decays as exp(−2κ m² t) (tested in tests/).

layers.title: References
items: Ottino, J.M. (1989). The Kinematics of Mixing: Stretching, Chaos, and Transport. Cambridge.

mix_stir.name: Dye: Stirring Only
mix_stir.question: How much variance does the numerical scheme lose without physical diffusion?

layers.title: The question
layers.text: How much variance does the numerical scheme lose without physical diffusion?

layers.title: What the colours and motion show
layers.text: The same stirring with κ = 0. A conserved dye should keep its variance; the decay seen is numerical diffusion of the bilinear semi-Lagrangian advection.

layers.title: One change to try
items: Raise the resolution: the numerical decay slows.

layers.title: What to measure
layers.text: The variance curve: its decay is entirely numerical.

layers.title: Physical explanation
layers.text: With κ = 0 the dye is a conserved passive scalar: stirring stretches and folds it into finer filaments without changing its variance in exact arithmetic. The decay seen is the numerical diffusion of the bilinear semi-Lagrangian advection once filaments reach the grid scale — a floor of the scheme, reported rather than hidden.

layers.title: Equations, symbols and assumptions
layers.text:
• c — the dye concentration (a passive scalar; it does not affect the flow)
• u — the turbulent velocity stirring it, from the spectral solver
• (u·∇)c — advection: the flow carrying the dye and stretching it into filaments
• κ∇²c — molecular diffusion, small, smoothing only the very finest filaments
• ∇·u = 0 — the stirring flow is incompressible (area-preserving)

layers.title: Initial and boundary conditions (this preset)
layers.ic: Alternating dye bands in the random stirring flow of the chosen seed.
layers.bc: Periodic in both directions; molecular diffusion switched off.

layers.title: Numerical method, checks and limitations
layers.text: The turbulent velocity comes from the same spectral vorticity solver; the dye is a passive scalar advected by it with periodic bilinear semi-Lagrangian transport (unconditionally stable) and a touch of spectral diffusion.
layers.checks: Numerical check (a measured floor of the scheme, reported rather than hidden).

layers.title: References
items: Ottino, J.M. (1989). The Kinematics of Mixing: Stretching, Chaos, and Transport. Cambridge.

mix_bands.name: Chaotic Mixing of Dye
mix_bands.question: How much apparent mixing comes from stirring and how much from diffusion?

layers.title: The question
layers.text: How much apparent mixing comes from stirring and how much from diffusion?

layers.title: What the colours and motion show
layers.text: Stripes of dye in a turbulent flow are stretched and folded into ever-finer filaments. Stirring alone cannot reduce the variance of a conserved dye; diffusion — physical and numerical — does.

layers.title: One change to try
items: Open the Diffusion Only scene (stirring 0) and the Stirring Only scene (κ = 0) and compare the variance curves.

layers.title: What to measure
layers.text: The dye variance versus time in the diagnostics.

layers.title: Physical explanation
layers.text:
Stir a drop of cream into coffee and it doesn't simply diffuse — the swirls stretch it into long thin ribbons, fold them over, stretch again, until the ribbons are so fine that the last bit of molecular diffusion finishes the job in an instant. This is chaotic advection: mixing done by the flow's stretching and folding, not by diffusion. It is exponentially faster than diffusion alone, which is why stirring works.

Here a turbulent 2-D velocity field (from the same spectral solver as the cloud billows) carries a passive dye that starts as clean stripes. The dye doesn't change the flow — it just goes along for the ride — so it traces the flow's invisible stretching, revealing the filamentary, self-similar structure that chaotic stirring always produces. The same process disperses pollutants in the ocean, ash in the atmosphere, and plankton across the sea surface.

Because the dye is merely transported, total dye is conserved as the filaments thin — mixing redistributes, it doesn't create or destroy.

layers.title: Equations, symbols and assumptions
layers.text:
• c — the dye concentration (a passive scalar; it does not affect the flow)
• u — the turbulent velocity stirring it, from the spectral solver
• (u·∇)c — advection: the flow carrying the dye and stretching it into filaments
• κ∇²c — molecular diffusion, small, smoothing only the very finest filaments
• ∇·u = 0 — the stirring flow is incompressible (area-preserving)

layers.title: Initial and boundary conditions (this preset)
layers.ic: A smooth random vorticity field stirring blobs of passive dye.
layers.bc: Periodic in both directions (pseudo-spectral); the dye is advected by, but does not alter, the flow.

layers.title: Numerical method, checks and limitations
layers.text: The turbulent velocity comes from the same spectral vorticity solver; the dye is a passive scalar advected by it with periodic bilinear semi-Lagrangian transport (unconditionally stable) and a touch of spectral diffusion.
layers.checks: Qualitative demonstration: the semi-Lagrangian scheme adds numerical diffusion once filaments reach the grid scale; the three scenes separate the contributions.

layers.title: References
items: Ottino, J.M. (1989). The Kinematics of Mixing: Stretching, Chaos, and Transport. Cambridge.

bands.label: Dye bands
bands.help: How many horizontal stripes of dye to start with.

diffusion.label: Dye diffusivity κ
diffusion.help: Molecular diffusion of the dye — higher blurs the fine filaments sooner. 0 = pure stirring (only numerical diffusion remains).

stir.label: Stirring strength
stir.help: Multiplies the stirring velocity: 1 = the full turbulent flow, 0 = diffusion only (compare how much mixing comes from stirring versus diffusion).

seed.label: Random seed
seed.help: Seed of the random stirring flow.

resolution.label: Resolution
resolution.help: Grid resolution. It changes the grid, and with it whatever a scene ties to the grid: the elapsed convective time in the wind tunnel, the Rayleigh number in the convection scenes, the grain size in the rock, the extent of the blast box. The derived readouts say what moved for this experiment; runs at different resolutions are comparable only where they say so.

duration.label: Duration (×)
duration.help: Simulated interval as a multiple of the scene's reference interval (1.0 = default).

compare.text: Diffusion alone versus stirring with diffusion from the same initial bands.
Stirring alone (numerical diffusion only) versus stirring with physical diffusion.
